description: AI & Full-Stack Developer (CS Senior) experienced in health-tech ML and real-time telemetry. Skilled in Python, Next.js, FastAPI, and RAG pipelines.
summary:
AstroVitals (.health) is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical AI platform engineered for deep-space missions where communication delays make Earth-based telemedicine impossible. During transit to Mars, speed-of-light radio signals take up to 22 minutes each way (44 minutes round-trip), preventing real-time emergency consultations while astronauts face microgravity bone loss (1–1.5% monthly), cephalad fluid shifts, Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and cosmic radiation storms.

AstroVitals addresses this challenge by deploying an autonomous AI Flight Surgeon directly at the spacecraft edge. It continuously ingests biometric telemetry into TimescaleDB time-series hypertables, plots vital trends against NASA-STD-3001 safe corridor bands, and provides an interactive 6-region anatomical body map that guides astronauts through step-by-step physical self-examinations (such as optic nerve ultrasound and blood pressure checks). Powered by Google Gemini 3.8 Flash grounded in NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) multi-omics baselines, AstroVitals delivers deterministic, hallucination-free clinical triage, gamified daily countermeasure quests, and automated emergency escalation without relying on Earth.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

AstroVitals operates as an onboard space medicine operating system. Biometric sensors stream continuous vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, HRV, blood glucose, core temperature, SpO2, sleep, and radiation dosimetry) into a local PostgreSQL database with TimescaleDB continuous aggregates (time_bucket('1 hour', recorded_at)). The frontend displays an interactive SVG anatomical body map with dynamic color-coded status badges (Nominal, Caution, Critical). Clicking any organ opens a Guided Self-Exam & Physiology Drawer with instructions for physical onboard diagnostics. When anomalies occur, the backend combines live telemetry with Inspiration4 multi-omics baselines (OSD-575, OSD-656, OSD-53) and queries a PostgreSQL pgvector(768) table of NASA/CSA clinical protocols. Google Gemini 3.8 Flash evaluates the multi-system evidence to return structured JSON containing clinical risk scores (0–100), plain-language diagnoses, prioritized countermeasure checklists, and explicit escalation thresholds.

What benefits does it have?

  • Complete Diagnostic Autonomy: Empowers astronauts to identify, verify, and treat medical issues independently during interplanetary blackouts.
  • Actionable Self-Examinations: Bridges the gap between passive sensor readings and active clinical diagnosis by guiding astronauts through standardized exam protocols.
  • Multi-Omics Context: Cross-references macroscopic vitals with microscopic cellular biomarkers (cytokines and gene expression) to distinguish benign microgravity adaptation from acute medical emergencies.
  • Behavioral Health Reinforcement: Gamified daily quests maintain crew morale and adherence to mandatory 60-minute daily resistive exercise (ARED) and circadian light hygiene.

What is the intended impact of the project?

AstroVitals eliminates single-point medical failure modes on crewed lunar (Artemis) and Martian missions. On Earth, this same offline edge-computing intelligence can deliver expert medical diagnostics to remote arctic research stations, maritime vessels, military deployments, and rural healthcare deserts devoid of internet connectivity.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript), React, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Recharts, Lucide Icons.
  • Backend API: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy, asyncpg.
  • Database (Tiger Data): PostgreSQL 16 with timescaledb (hypertables and continuous aggregate rollups) and pgvector (768-dimensional vector cosine distance search).
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API (gemini-3.8-flash for structured clinical evaluation and text-embedding-004 for protocol vector embeddings).
  • Authentication: Auth0 Next.js SDK and FastAPI JWT bearer verification enforcing 3-Role RBAC (astronaut, crew_medical_officer, flight_surgeon).
  • Emergency Communications: Twilio Python SDK for programmable SMS, WhatsApp, and Voice call escalation, tested via the Twilio Dev Phone.
  • Infrastructure & Deployment: Multi-stage Dockerfiles, Docker Compose, Caddy reverse proxy with automated Let's Encrypt TLS, pre-configured for Vultr Cloud and custom GoDaddy domain routing (astrovitals.health).

How is your project creative?

  1. Interactive Guided Self-Exam Drawer: Instead of simply presenting graphs, clicking an affected body system provides illustrated, step-by-step physical self-exam protocols (e.g., optic nerve ultrasound for SANS) with clear escalation thresholds.
  2. Mars OWLT Delay Simulator: An interactive toggle switch demonstrating the real-world difference between 0-second Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and 22-minute Mars speed-of-light communication lag, visually validating why on-device AI is non-negotiable.
  3. Macro-to-Micro Data Fusion: Uniquely synthesizes macroscopic vital signs with microscopic spaceflight omics data (Inspiration4 cytokines and RNA expression).
  4. Gamified Countermeasure Hub: Transforms mandatory resistive exercise into an RPG-style quest progression with XP and streak rewards to combat deep-space psychological fatigue.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Interplanetary Physics: Speed-of-light radio latency (3 to 22 minutes each way).
  • Zero-Connectivity Operations: The entire platform runs self-contained inside the habitat cluster without requiring external internet.
  • AI Safety & Hallucination Prevention: Strict Pydantic response_schema enforcement combined with vector RAG grounding in official NASA-STD-3001 and CSA guidelines.
  • Astronaut Human Factors: Minimal cognitive load, high-contrast dark space UI, and non-invasive diagnostic workflows feasible in zero-gravity.
